suggestion: Refresh the pinned upstream snapshot on a fixed weekly cadence and mark the line board 'expired' once the kickoff of the earliest listed game has passed.
problem: The published pin was 2026-11-02. Until this session refreshed it, the 'upcoming' board still listed Week 8-9 games that had already been played, and the ratings were missing two weeks of results.
benefit: The originated lines always refer to unplayed games; the model's ratings are never more than one week old.
cost: One pinned fetch plus a full rebuild and re-verification per week (about 3 minutes of compute, plus a re-run of the audit).
risk: Every published number moves at each refresh. Without an archive of prior builds, week-to-week comparisons become impossible.
evidence_status: PARTIALLY DEMONSTRATED in this session: the refresh was executed and the pipeline rebuilt; the weekly cadence itself is not automated.

suggestion: Extend the injury + depth-chart register from the 6 pilot clubs to all 32 clubs, and add the missing clubs in the order their games kick off.
problem: The register covers 3 of the 16 Week 10 games. 26 clubs have no depth-verified row, so no league-wide deficiency measure exists.
benefit: A complete, source-linked availability ledger for every club, which is the minimum input for any availability-adjusted line.
cost: 26 additional club-depth-chart reads per refresh, each of which must be transcribed and checked.
risk: Club charts change daily and are labelled UNOFFICIAL by at least three clubs; a stale chart silently becomes a wrong starter label.
evidence_status: PILOT ONLY: 6 clubs verified, 26 explicitly flagged as not covered.

suggestion: Replace projected depth-chart ranks with official pre-kickoff inactives (published about 90 minutes before kickoff) and post-game snap counts, keeping the chart only as the prior.
problem: A depth chart says who is expected to start, not who did. Every 'starter out' statement in this register is a projection from a club chart, and three clubs label those charts unofficial.
benefit: The deficiency measure becomes an observation of the actual lineup rather than an inference about it.
cost: One inactives read per game plus a snap-count source; both must be archived with a timestamp to survive retroactive edits.
risk: Inactives arrive too late to price a bet, and no official snap-count feed has been verified in this repository yet.
evidence_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. The limitation is stated on every row of the register.

suggestion: Add a starter-availability differential as a candidate feature in the walk-forward model, and let it enter only if it passes the existing eight gates.
problem: The model currently has no availability input, so a lineup deficiency cannot move an originated line.
benefit: A testable, mechanism-based signal instead of a hunch; the gate structure already prevents a lucky fit from shipping.
cost: Requires a multi-season 32-club availability history, which does not exist yet (S02/S03 are prerequisites).
risk: Availability data is retrospective-friendly and leak-prone: the injury report is published during the week, so the model must use only the pre-kickoff snapshot or it will look prescient.
evidence_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED; blocked on S02 and S03.

suggestion: Acquire timestamped, authenticated sportsbook quotes (open, close, limits) and store them with a licence note.
problem: Eight gates fail closed on G1 because no executable price provenance exists. ROI and CLV cannot be computed from a community mirror.
benefit: Unblocks the only evidence class that can turn a backtest into a defensible edge claim.
cost: Commercial data licence or manual timestamped capture; both are recurring costs.
risk: Vendor prices can be restated, and a mirror is still not a ticket. The store must keep the received bytes and receipt time.

suggestion: Freeze a prospective paper-trading window: register every rule, price source and stake before the first game, then publish the untouched result.
problem: Every result in the repository is a backtest. The complete search history is unknown, so a good backtest cannot be separated from selection.
benefit: A single pre-registered test is stronger evidence than any further backtest tuning.
cost: A full NFL season of elapsed time, or a shortened window with an honest power statement.
risk: Rules drift during the season unless the registry is committed and hashed before kickoff.

suggestion: Replace the provisional deflated Sharpe ratio with a complete trial registry count and publish the count next to every p-value.
problem: The deflated Sharpe needs the number of trials. Only a lower bound of 60 is known, so the correction is acknowledged as provisional.
benefit: Multiplicity correction becomes auditable instead of assumed.
cost: Low: a registry file plus a commit hook that appends every configuration tried.
risk: A registry only helps if abandoned trials are recorded too; silent retries would restore the bias.
evidence_status: PARTIALLY: trial_count_lower_bound = 60 is published; the registry does not exist.
reference_label: Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014), deflated Sharpe

suggestion: Obtain verified player-prop prices and same-game-parlay joint quotes before publishing any prop-combo ROI.
problem: Prop lines are calculated; ticket prices and joint quotes are absent, so no prop ROI is claimed.
benefit: Turns the dependence research into an executable test and makes the correlation work decision-relevant.
cost: A prop-price archive with timestamps and an operator-specific joint-price capture.
risk: SGP pricing is operator-specific; a generic correlation adjustment can disagree with the actual ticket price.
evidence_status: BLOCKED: no prop prices or joint quotes in the repository.

suggestion: Make the verification suite a required check on every pull request, including the new injury invariants (official source per row, hash match, no inferred depth rank).
problem: Fail-closed checks exist but nothing in the workflow enforces them for future sessions beyond the current CI job.
benefit: A future edit cannot silently publish an unsourced row or an inferred starter.
cost: Low: extend the existing verify workflow with the new test file.
risk: A flaky network fetch inside CI would block merges; checks must run on committed snapshots only.
evidence_status: PARTIAL: CI already runs the verifier; the injury partition was added in this session and is wired into make test and the workflow.

suggestion: Add a machine-readable decision log (JSON) next to this page so each suggestion's status, evidence and chosen path can be diffed in git.
problem: Decisions are currently prose in COORDINATION.md, which is long and hard to audit.
benefit: Every accepted or rejected path has a dated, reviewable record.
cost: Low: one schema plus the renderer already built for this page.
risk: A log that is updated only at the end of a project is not a decision log. It must be edited when the decision is made.
evidence_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED; this page is the first human-readable version.

suggestion: Split the coordination log into dated files and keep COORDINATION.md as the task board plus a short index.
problem: The board is a single growing file of more than 1,000 lines, and three recorded merge conflicts were caused by concurrent appends to it.
benefit: Fewer conflicts between parallel sessions and a readable board.
cost: Low: a one-time split; links must be updated.
risk: History can be lost if the split is done with a rewrite rather than an append-only move.

suggestion: Publish an explicit no-bet default and a kill-switch that voids every reward if a validated strategy is later found to rely on unavailable or restated prices.
problem: The leaderboard has no reward, but nothing formal says what happens if a strategy passes and the price provenance is later challenged.
benefit: Protects the credibility of the competition and the operator.
cost: Low: a policy paragraph and a data-integrity trigger.
risk: Over-broad invalidation could discard genuine results; the trigger must be specific and documented.
evidence_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED; the current policy is 'no reward without validation'.

suggestion: After each refresh, publish the model-versus-market paired error table with the change from the previous refresh, so improvements are visible as deltas.
problem: Model error is published as a level, not as a change, so a regression after a data refresh is invisible.
benefit: Makes the effect of data refreshes and feature changes reviewable over time.
cost: Low: keep the prior refresh's metrics in a dated file.
risk: Paired samples differ after a refresh; the delta must be computed on a fixed game set.
evidence_status: NOT IMPLEMENTED; this session refreshed the pin and the paired errors moved (see the audit page).
